skill.name: rust-pro
skill.description: Master Rust 1.75+ with modern async patterns, advanced type system features, and production-ready systems programming. Expert in the latest Rust ecosystem including Tokio, axum, and cutting-edge crates. Use PROACTIVELY for Rust development, performance optimization, or systems programming.
skill.summary: Advanced Rust guidance for async services, systems programming, safety, testing, and performance.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The single static finding appears to be a false positive. The cited lines describe Rust type-system behavior and memory-safety priorities, with no network reconnaissance intent or instructions.

static_findings.snippet: - Leverages the type system for compile-time correctness

finding_verdicts.reason: Lines 137-138 describe compile-time correctness and memory safety as Rust development traits. There is no request to scan networks, enumerate hosts, or perform reconnaissance.

content.value_statement: Rust projects often require careful choices across ownership, async runtimes, safety, and performance. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through production Rust design and implementation.
actual_capabilities: Designs Rust services, libraries, and systems tooling with ownership and lifetime guidance.
Explains async Rust patterns with Tokio, axum, tower, hyper, streams, and channels.
Improves performance through memory layout, zero-cost abstractions, profiling, and cache-aware design.
Guides testing with unit tests, integration tests, property-based tests, benchmarks, and documentation tests.
Plans safer unsafe-code and FFI boundaries with documented invariants and minimal unsafe blocks.
Recommends Cargo tooling for formatting, linting, dependency review, workspaces, and publishing.
limitations: It does not execute Rust code or verify compiler output without an available local toolchain.
It may need current crate documentation for newly released Rust ecosystem changes.
It cannot guarantee performance gains without benchmarks, profiles, and representative workloads.
It should not replace a security review for unsafe code, FFI, cryptography, or production networking.

use_cases.title: Design Async Services
use_cases.description: Plan an axum, tower, or Tokio service with structured errors, middleware, tests, and backpressure.

use_cases.title: Resolve Ownership Problems
use_cases.description: Untangle lifetime, borrowing, trait-bound, and generic design issues in complex Rust modules.

use_cases.title: Harden Systems Code
use_cases.description: Review unsafe blocks, FFI wrappers, allocators, and low-level I/O designs for clearer safety invariants.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a Rust Error
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner support for compiler or borrow-checker errors.
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain this Rust compiler error in plain language. Show the ownership or lifetime issue, then suggest a minimal fix.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Async Service
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate planning for a web service or API.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Rust async service for this requirement. Choose Tokio, axum, or related crates, and outline modules, errors, tests, and runtime concerns.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize a Hot Path
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced performance review for existing Rust logic.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Rust hot path for memory layout, allocation, concurrency, and cache behavior. Recommend measurable optimizations and benchmark strategy.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Unsafe Boundaries
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert review for unsafe code or FFI.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this unsafe Rust or FFI design. Identify required safety invariants, lifetime assumptions, aliasing risks, and a safer public API.

output_examples.input: Design a high-performance async web service with proper error handling.
output_examples.output: A service architecture with crate choices, route layout, typed errors, middleware, test strategy, and deployment considerations.

output_examples.input: Optimize this Rust code for better memory usage and cache locality.
output_examples.output: A performance review covering allocation sources, data layout options, profiling steps, and benchmark targets.

output_examples.input: Create a safe wrapper around a C library using FFI.
output_examples.output: A wrapper design with ownership rules, lifetime boundaries, error mapping, unsafe invariants, and validation tests.

best_practices: Provide compiler errors, relevant code, Cargo features, target platform, and runtime constraints.
Ask for tests, benchmarks, and linting plans when requesting implementation guidance.
State safety, latency, memory, and compatibility requirements before selecting crates or APIs.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for unsafe optimizations without documenting safety invariants.
Do not request broad rewrites when a focused ownership, API, or performance issue is known.
Do not accept performance advice without measurements on representative workloads.

faq.question: Does this skill support async Rust?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers Tokio, streams, channels, axum, tower, hyper, and common concurrency patterns.

faq.question: Can it help with borrow-checker errors?
faq.answer: Yes. It can explain ownership, borrowing, lifetime, and trait-bound problems with practical fixes.

faq.question: Does it write production-ready code?
faq.answer: It is designed to guide production code, including errors, tests, linting, and documentation. Local validation is still required.

faq.question: Can it review unsafe Rust?
faq.answer: Yes. It can identify required invariants and safer API boundaries, but it should not replace expert security review.

faq.question: Which tools does it work with?
faq.answer: It is suitable for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Does it require network access?
faq.answer: No. The skill content itself is guidance-only and does not include commands that require network access.
